newsitem.title: USA: Michigan's jobless rate drops in August.
newsitem.headline: Michigan's jobless rate drops in August.

text.p: Michigan's unemployment rate for August dropped to 4.5 percent, the Michigan Employment Security Commission reported Wednesday.
The state's seasonally adjusted jobless rate had crept up to 4.8 percent in July due to a temporary decline in auto industry-related employment.
In August, 217,000 Michigan residents were unemployed, compared to 232,000 in July. In August 1995, the state's unemployment rate was 5.2 percent with 250,000 people out of work.

"A sure sign of strength in Michigan's economy is the amount of job growth over the year," said employment security commission director F. Robert Edwards in a news release. "Since last August, employment has mushroomed by 140,000, while the workforce has risen by 108,000. At the same time, unemployment has dropped by 33,000."
